This masks the original type of\\nnon-authorization failures and prevents callers from distinguishing authorization\\nfailures from lookup or setup failures.\\n\\n**Actual Behavior**\\n\\n`authenticate` converts every `setupContext` failure into `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n**Expected Behavior**\\n\\n`authenticate` must preserve the distinction between access-related and unrelated\\nerrors:\\n\\n- An authorization failure and an unsupported user type are access-related and\\n  must be returned as `AccessDenied` (`trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == true`).\\n- An unknown Kubernetes cluster in the local cluster is not access-related and\\n  must remain a non-`AccessDenied` lookup/not-found-style error.\\n- A remote-cluster request made by a process without a reverse tunnel is not\\n  access-related. The underlying `setupContext` error is `BadParameter`; it must\\n  remain non-`AccessDenied` (`trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == false`).\\n- Non-access errors may be wrapped, but their trace classification must be\\n  preserved.\\n\\n\\nREQUIREMENTS:\\n- `authenticate` must return `AccessDenied` only when the underlying failure is\\n  access- or authorization-related.\\n\\n- The following cases must satisfy `trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == true`:\\n  - an authorization failure reported by the authorization layer;\\n  - an unsupported user type in the resolved authentication context.\\n\\n- The following cases must satisfy `trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == false`:\\n  - an unknown Kubernetes cluster referenced in the local cluster;\\n  - a remote-cluster request that cannot be served because the current process has\\n    no reverse tunnel. This case originates as `trace.BadParameter` and must not be\\n    reclassified as `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n- When `setupContext` returns a non-access error, `authenticate` must preserve or\\n  wrap the original error rather than replacing it with `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n- The implementation must not change `setupContext` merely to force a desired\\n  classification at the caller. This masks the original type of\\nnon-authorization failures and prevents callers from distinguishing authorization\\nfailures from lookup or setup failures.\\n\\n**Actual Behavior**\\n\\n`authenticate` converts every `setupContext` failure into `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n**Expected Behavior**\\n\\n`authenticate` must preserve the distinction between access-related and unrelated\\nerrors:\\n\\n- An authorization failure and an unsupported user type are access-related and\\n  must be returned as `AccessDenied` (`trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == true`).\\n- An unknown Kubernetes cluster in the local cluster is not access-related and\\n  must remain a non-`AccessDenied` lookup/not-found-style error.\\n- A remote-cluster request made by a process without a reverse tunnel is not\\n  access-related. The underlying `setupContext` error is `BadParameter`; it must\\n  remain non-`AccessDenied` (`trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == false`).\\n- Non-access errors may be wrapped, but their trace classification must be\\n  preserved.\\n\\n\\nREQUIREMENTS:\\n- `authenticate` must return `AccessDenied` only when the underlying failure is\\n  access- or authorization-related.\\n\\n- The following cases must satisfy `trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == true`:\\n  - an authorization failure reported by the authorization layer;\\n  - an unsupported user type in the resolved authentication context.\\n\\n- The following cases must satisfy `trace.IsAccessDenied(err) == false`:\\n  - an unknown Kubernetes cluster referenced in the local cluster;\\n  - a remote-cluster request that cannot be served because the current process has\\n    no reverse tunnel. This case originates as `trace.BadParameter` and must not be\\n    reclassified as `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n- When `setupContext` returns a non-access error, `authenticate` must preserve or\\n  wrap the original error rather than replacing it with `AccessDenied`.\\n\\n- The implementation must not change `setupContext` merely to force a desired\\n  classification at the caller.
